result.content:
# Proposed discovery plan

Decide whether to invest in building a handoff tracking tool specifically targeted at small software engineering teams in Latvia.

## Proposed scope

- Investigating handoff workflows and coordination overhead in small software teams in Latvia.
- Evaluating demand for automated or structured handoff tracking versus existing general-purpose tools.
- Excluding payroll, accounting, and financial advisory functionality.

Region: Latvia

Explicit exclusions: Do not include payroll or financial advice

## Engineering Lead

Oversees engineering delivery, weekly coordination, and cross-developer handoffs.

- How many hours per week do team members typically spend documenting and syncing handoff updates? (question-a778b32070343d2fc5d990c8)
- Which tools and workflows are currently relied on for status handoffs, and what friction occurs? (question-fcd273ad26b2efbb843d83b0)

## Product Manager

Coordinates cross-functional milestones, release tracking, and operational transitions.

- Under what conditions would your team adopt and budget for a dedicated handoff tracker rather than existing project management tools? (question-5589a2a5620866e8a82d2282)

## Simulation hypotheses

- We spend two hours copying handoff updates each Friday. [source:operator-interview]

## Assumptions

- Small software teams in Latvia experience recurring manual overhead during weekly project handoffs.
- Teams may prefer a dedicated handoff solution over general-purpose issue trackers or chat tools.

## Evidence gaps

- No verified empirical data exists on market size or willingness to pay for handoff tracking software among Latvian software firms.
- Evidence is limited to a synthetic fixture; no real customer interviews or market pricing studies have been conducted.
- No non-synthetic source findings were established; the plan is a proposal, not customer validation.

This scope is proposed, not a claim of user approval.

## Selected sources

- [source:operator-interview] Synthetic operator interview fixture — synthetic_transcript
